title: Getting started with directeffect
text: Comparative-effectiveness studies mostly estimate relative effects: drug versus drug B active-comparator design. estimate constrains difference two drugs’ latent direct effects. researcher ultimately wants drug’s direct effect versus placebo — almost none evidence speaks directly. directeffect reconstructs direct effects network comparative estimates, keeping two questions deliberately separate: surface. comparative estimates internally coherent, relative structure imply? Comparisons alone answer . sea level. structure sit relative placebo = 0? absolute (placebo-anchored) evidence answers . API mirrors separation: direct_effect_network() → fit_surface() → anchor_surface().

what: The problem: we measure differences, but we want heights
title: How directeffect works
text: Imagine want know tall three friends , measuring stick broken: can measure difference two people standing back back, never anyone’s actual height. Alice vs. Bob: exactly height. Alice vs. Carol: Alice 4 cm taller. Bob vs. Carol: Bob 4 cm taller. three measurements know shape lineup perfectly — Alice Bob level, Carol 4 cm — idea whether Carol 150 cm 190 cm. Every height shifted amount three measurements still exactly right. Drug safety evidence structure. studies compare one drug another drug (drug vs. drug B), comparing drug treatment often impossible unethical run. study measures difference two drugs, drug’s effect. number actually want — drug’s direct effect, effect versus taking placebo — like actual height. leads trap worth naming: null comparison mean two safe drugs. “Alice vs. Bob: height” also true standing table.

what: The fix: one measurement against the floor
title: How directeffect works
text: just one friend ever measured floor, every height snaps place. Say proper measurement shows Carol 160 cm. Alice Bob 164 cm — even though one ever measured either directly. drug terms, “measurement floor” placebo-controlled trial. directeffect calls anchor, calls floor sea level (placebo = 0). package works two deliberate steps: surface: use drug-vs-drug comparisons work shape — every drug’s position relative others. sea level: use placebo-controlled anchors slide whole shape true absolute position. friends example data. Effects log hazard ratio scale — 0 means “effect”, bigger means harmful — arithmetic heights: -vs-B comparison exactly null, yet drugs come 0.7 placebo. null comparison told us B sit height; anchor C told us high .
code: library(directeffect)  comparisons <- data.frame(   study_id   = c("S1", "S2", "S3"),   target     = c("A", "A", "B"),   comparator = c("B", "C", "C"),   estimate   = c(0.0, 0.4, 0.4),   # A vs B is null!   std_error  = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05) ) anchors <- data.frame(   study_id  = "RCT1",   drug      = "C",   reference = "placebo",   estimate  = 0.3,               # C measured against the floor   std_error = 0.04 )  de <- direct_effect_network(comparisons, anchors = anchors,                             effect_measure = "HR") absolute <- anchor_surface(fit_surface(de, engine = "netmeta")) absolute$effects[, c("drug", "estimate", "std_error")] #>   drug estimate  std_error #> 1    A      0.7 0.05715476 #> 2    B      0.7 0.05715476 #> 3    C      0.3 0.04000000

title: How directeffect works
text: Real studies noisy: measure pair twice get two slightly different answers, going around loop (vs. B, B vs. C, C vs. ) may sum exactly zero. package just chain measurements together — find heights fit measurements , closely possible. idea taking average, two refinements: Least squares. Choose set heights whose predicted differences come closest observed differences. measurements conflict, answer lands , way average . Weighting. study small standard error careful measurement; one large standard error rough one. measurement counts proportion 1 / std_error^2, careful studies pull harder answer. Anchoring works way: placebo trial proposes “slide surface much”, proposals combined weighted average — anchors’ uncertainty kept, imprecise placebo trial gives imprecise absolute effects, . Every reported estimate carries standard error 95% interval built uncertainty together.

title: How directeffect works
text: package ships simulated statin evidence base: twelve head--head trials among six statins three placebo-controlled trials, generated invented, known truth (example_truth) realistic noise added. Real drug names, fake numbers — exactly makes useful : can run full method grade answer key. Line estimates truth data generated : Three things check table: estimates miss truth hundredths log scale — noise simulated , flaw — every interval covers true value, package recovers true ranking six drugs. None six measured placebo , three never measured placebo ; absolute effects come entirely network plus anchors.  grading one-: package’s test suite re-runs (many stricter versions ) every commit.
code: de <- direct_effect_network(   example_comparisons,   anchors = example_anchors,   effect_measure = "HR" ) absolute <- anchor_surface(fit_surface(de, engine = "netmeta")) truth <- example_truth$theta[match(absolute$effects$drug,                                    example_truth$drug)] report <- data.frame(   drug      = absolute$effects$drug,   estimated = round(absolute$effects$estimate, 3),   true      = truth,   error     = round(absolute$effects$estimate - truth, 3),   lower     = round(absolute$effects$lower, 3),   upper     = round(absolute$effects$upper, 3) ) report[order(report$estimated), ] #>           drug estimated  true  error  lower  upper #> 5 rosuvastatin    -0.423 -0.32 -0.103 -0.533 -0.314 #> 1 atorvastatin    -0.324 -0.30 -0.024 -0.420 -0.227 #> 6  simvastatin    -0.278 -0.26 -0.018 -0.367 -0.189 #> 4  pravastatin    -0.190 -0.22  0.030 -0.285 -0.094 #> 3   lovastatin    -0.129 -0.20  0.071 -0.287  0.029 #> 2  fluvastatin    -0.094 -0.17  0.076 -0.241  0.054 # 1. Every 95% interval contains the true value. all(report$lower <= report$true & report$true <= report$upper) #> [1] TRUE  # 2. The estimated ordering of the six statins is exactly the true #    ordering. cor(report$estimated, report$true, method = "spearman") #> [1] 1  # 3. The typical error is about the size the standard errors promised. sqrt(mean(report$error^2)) #> [1] 0.06221736 plot_sea_level(absolute)
